author: HSinghHira
description:
Coder turns a spare machine into a cloud development platform: spin up full development environments that open straight in your browser or your favorite local IDE, think a self-hosted GitHub Codespaces.

**Features**

- Browser-based development environments and terminal, no local
  setup required.

- Connect from VS Code, JetBrains, or any SSH-compatible editor.
- Reproducible workspaces defined as code (Terraform-based
  templates).

- Works great on a home network out of the box, and scales up to a
  full public, HTTPS, single-sign-on deployment.

- Optional sign-in through Pocket ID via OpenID Connect (OIDC),
  alongside Coder's own built-in username/password accounts.

- PostgreSQL 17 for persistent application data.
- Persistent storage under /DATA/AppData/$AppID.

**How to use?**

1. Open Coder from the Zima OS dashboard.
2. The first time you open it, create your administrator account
   right in the browser.

3. Explore the Templates tab and start from a starter template, or
   import one of your own.

4. Create a workspace from a template to get a full browser IDE and
   terminal.

5. Optionally connect your local VS Code or JetBrains IDE to the
   same workspace over SSH.

6. If you want centralized sign-in, set up Pocket ID as described in
   this app's README, then fill in the OIDC settings and restart
   Coder.

7. Ongoing settings (users, groups, SSO, templates) are managed from
   Coder's own Admin area in the web UI after install.

tips.before_install:
1. Open the app's settings before you start the install.

2. Find CODER_ACCESS_URL. This is the address people will type to
   open Coder.


3. For home-only use, set it to http://<your-device-IP>:8448. Swap
   in your device's real LAN IP.


4. For internet use, set it to your real domain, like
   https://coder.example.com. You will also need a reverse proxy
   with HTTPS in front of Coder. See the README for examples.


5. CODER_PG_CONNECTION_URL is already filled in with a random
   database password. Leave it alone unless you know what you are
   doing.


6. If you do change the password inside CODER_PG_CONNECTION_URL,
   change POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the postgres service to match, or
   Coder cannot start.


7. Want Pocket ID sign-in? Fill in CODER_OIDC_ISSUER_URL,
   CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, and CODER_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET. If not,
   leave all three blank and skip to step 9.


8. Set the Pocket ID redirect URL to
   <your-access-url>/api/v2/users/oidc/callback before you start
   Coder, or Pocket ID sign-in will fail.


9. Start the Coder installation.

10. Wait about a minute for Coder and its database to finish
    starting up.


11. Open Coder from the Zima OS dashboard.

12. The first person to open Coder creates the admin account
    right there in the browser.


13. More settings (users, groups, templates, SSO) live inside
    Coder's own Admin area after install, or by editing this
    app's environment variables and restarting.


14. Important: only turn on CODER_DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH after
    you've signed in with Pocket ID successfully at least once.
    Turning it on too early can lock everyone out.

title: Coder
release_note:
- Initial version.
- Pinned to Coder v2.35.6 (stable release channel).
- PostgreSQL 17 backend, internal-only, healthcheck-gated startup.
- Optional Pocket ID / OIDC sign-in alongside built-in password auth.
- Docker socket is intentionally not mounted; see README for
  enabling Docker-based workspaces.
